summary.headline: Settings insight and Autopilot known-issues guidance are refreshed
summary.overview: The day is primarily a documentation maintenance release spanning Settings insight, Windows Autopilot known issues, Apple update guidance, Managed Home Screen actions, and Configuration Manager SQL replication.
summary.adminImpact: No broad configuration change is evidenced. Use the latest known-issues and Settings insight articles when troubleshooting, and keep support runbooks aligned with the current Managed Home Screen and Apple update references.

keyChanges.title: Windows Autopilot known issues are updated
keyChanges.detail: The known-issues reference receives a substantive update and remains the current source to check before escalating Autopilot deployment behavior as a tenant configuration issue.

keyChanges.title: Settings insight guidance is refreshed
keyChanges.detail: The Settings insight documentation is updated as part of the broader support-reference maintenance, giving administrators the latest source for interpreting and acting on configuration insights.

summary.headline: Apple profile references consolidate and retire older platform-specific pages
summary.overview: Apple custom-settings, feature, restrictions, VPN, and Wi-Fi documentation is refined while older iOS/iPadOS and macOS-specific pages are removed, continuing the migration to the focused Apple configuration references introduced the prior week.
summary.adminImpact: Update links in Apple administration runbooks to the consolidated Apple pages. Recheck any local guidance that points to deleted platform-specific profile articles, and continue to use built-in profiles for sensitive Wi-Fi and certificate settings.

keyChanges.title: Apple configuration documentation consolidates platform-specific content
keyChanges.detail: Older custom-settings, restrictions, device-features, VPN, and Wi-Fi pages for iOS/iPadOS and macOS are removed as content moves into the newer Apple-focused references.

keyChanges.title: Remote Help monitoring guidance is maintained
keyChanges.detail: The troubleshooting and monitoring reference receives an update, retaining the current support path for investigating Remote Help device-side behavior.

summary.headline: Inactive devices will be excluded from Intune reporting, while Cloud PKI and ConfigMgr updates land
summary.overview: The key operational change is a Message Center notice that Intune reporting will exclude devices inactive for 12 months or longer starting in late February. The day also updates Cloud PKI expiration guidance, Apple profile documentation, and introduces Configuration Manager hotfix articles.
summary.adminImpact: Prepare stakeholders for lower device counts in reports without assuming a fleet reduction; devices must check in to remain represented. Review dashboards, reports, and KPIs that compare historical counts. Validate applicable Configuration Manager hotfixes against your deployment version before installation.

keyChanges.title: Intune reporting will exclude devices inactive for 12 months
keyChanges.detail: From late February 2026, Intune reports exclude devices that have been inactive for 12 months or more, improving active-device accuracy. Counts can decrease; devices must check in to continue appearing.

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI CA-expiration guidance is updated
keyChanges.detail: The Cloud PKI runbook is refreshed to reinforce replacement issuing-CA and SCEP-profile planning before expiry interrupts new certificate issuance.

keyChanges.title: Connected Cache hotfix documentation is published for Configuration Manager 2603
keyChanges.detail: A new hotfix article adds the Connected Cache update reference for version 2603, giving Configuration Manager administrators a version-specific release record to assess.

summary.headline: EPM support and Android app-protection references receive targeted maintenance
summary.overview: The day updates Android app protection, Microsoft Edge, filters, Microsoft Tunnel, and Endpoint Privilege Management support documentation. The changes are primarily reference clarification, with no announced new enforcement or configuration capability.
summary.adminImpact: No immediate rollout is required. Use the refreshed EPM support and Android app-protection references when troubleshooting policy applicability, and review filters against the supported-workloads documentation before relying on a filter in production assignments.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint Privilege Management support reference is refreshed
keyChanges.detail: The EPM support documentation receives a targeted update, preserving the current source for supported scenarios and escalation checks.

keyChanges.title: Android app-protection settings are updated
keyChanges.detail: The Android app-protection policy settings reference receives two maintenance updates, keeping current configuration and behavior information available to app-protection administrators.

summary.headline: Defender vulnerability remediation and Windows enrollment guidance are clarified
summary.overview: A substantial update refreshes the guidance for using Intune to remediate vulnerabilities surfaced by Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. Related Windows enrollment and device-protection pages are maintained.
summary.adminImpact: Security and endpoint teams should validate their vulnerability-remediation workflow against the new guidance, including ownership between Defender findings and Intune deployment actions. Update enrollment documentation used by operators if it embeds older Windows automatic-enrollment steps.

keyChanges.title: Vulnerability remediation guidance is substantially revised
keyChanges.detail: The updated guide remains the central reference for taking vulnerability information from Microsoft Defender for Endpoint into Intune remediation actions and clarifies the supporting endpoint-security workflow.

keyChanges.title: Windows automatic-enrollment documentation is maintained
keyChanges.detail: The Windows enrollment article receives follow-up updates, keeping the current reference for enabling and operating MDM automatic enrollment.

summary.headline: February roadmap and January service update are announced
summary.overview: There are no tracked documentation-file changes, but two Message Center announcements publish the February Intune In Development roadmap and confirm the January 2026 Intune service update.
summary.adminImpact: Review the February roadmap with product owners and help desk teams to prepare for upcoming changes. Confirm the January release level in Tenant Status and reconcile any planned work with the latest What’s New documentation.

keyChanges.title: February 2026 Intune In Development roadmap is available
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft announces the updated February feature list to support organizational readiness for capabilities rolling out in the next month or later releases.

keyChanges.title: January 2026 Intune service update is announced
keyChanges.detail: The Message Center confirms the January service build and directs administrators to Tenant Status and What’s New for release details and readiness planning.

summary.headline: Configuration Manager state-message reference receives a small update
summary.overview: The only tracked change is a maintenance edit to the Configuration Manager state-messages documentation. No product behavior, policy, or rollout change is evidenced.
summary.adminImpact: No action is required. Use the current State Messages reference for Configuration Manager monitoring and troubleshooting procedures.

keyChanges.title: State Messages documentation is maintained
keyChanges.detail: The Configuration Manager state-messages reference receives a minor update and remains the current documentation source for interpreting client and deployment state reporting.

summary.headline: Reporting accuracy and service-readiness updates define the mid-February week
summary.overview: The week records 90 changes and three Message Center announcements. The most consequential item is Intune’s forthcoming exclusion of devices inactive for 12 months from reporting. The week also refreshes Apple configuration links, Defender vulnerability-remediation guidance, Cloud PKI continuity material, and publishes February roadmap and January service-update notices.
summary.adminImpact: Prepare reporting consumers for the late-February count change, verify key reports distinguish active inventory from historical records, and make check-in health part of device lifecycle operations. Review the new roadmap and service update, assess Configuration Manager hotfix applicability, and keep Defender remediation and Apple-profile runbooks current.

keyChanges.title: Inactive devices will be removed from Intune reports
keyChanges.detail: Starting late February, devices inactive for at least 12 months are excluded from reporting. This can reduce counts while improving representation of active devices.

keyChanges.title: Defender vulnerability remediation guidance is refreshed
keyChanges.detail: The substantially revised guide remains the operating reference for using Intune to remediate Microsoft Defender for Endpoint findings.

keyChanges.title: February in-development roadmap and January service update are announced
keyChanges.detail: Message Center publishes the February readiness roadmap and confirms the January Intune service build, directing teams to review What’s New and Tenant Status.

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI expiration and Configuration Manager hotfix information is updated
keyChanges.detail: The week updates the CA-expiration runbook and publishes Configuration Manager hotfix references, including a Connected Cache update for version 2603.
